content.text: To move a body or to bring it to rest or to change the velocity of a body, it needs a ‘push’ or ‘pull’.
This ‘push’ or ‘pull’ is called as ‘force’.
Motion refers to the change in position of a body over time.
The two types of motion are,
Natural Motion: Refers to the motion of body without any external force.
Violent Motion: Refers to the motion of body with an external force.
When dropped from certain height in vacuum, objects of different size, shape and mass fall at a same rate and reach the ground at the same time.
A moving object will continue to be in the same state of motion, unless an external force is applied.
The property of a body to resist any change in its state of rest or the state of uniform motion, unless it is influenced upon by an external unbalanced force, is known as ‘inertia’.
The linear momentum measures the impact of a force on a body.
The product of mass and velocity of a moving body gives the magnitude of linear momentum.
It acts in the direction of the velocity of the object.
Momentum helps to measure the magnitude of a force.

**1.1 - Inertia and Linear Momentum**
This law states that every body continues to be in its state of rest or the state of uniform motion along a straight line unless it is acted upon by some external force
Force is an external effort in the form of push or pull, which
Produces or tries to produce the motion of a static body
Stops or tries to stop a moving body
Changes or tries to change the direction of motion of a moving body
Force is a vector quantity as it has both magnitude and direction
Types of Forces
Resultant Force
When several forces act simultaneously on the same body, then the combined effect of the multiple forces can be represented by “resultant force”.
It is equal to the vector sum of all the forces.
Balanced and Unbalanced forces
The axis of the fixed edge about which an object is rotated is called as the ‘axis of rotation’

content.text: Couple
Two equal and unlike parallel forces applied simultaneously at two distinct points constitute a couple.
The line of action of the two forces does not coincide.
Rotating effect of a couple is known as moment of a couple.

Turning a tap
Winding or unwinding a screw
Spinning of a top

content.text: By Newton’s second law of motion,
No external force is required to maintain the motion of a body moving with uniform velocity.
When the net force acting on a body is not equal to zero, then the velocity of the body will change.
Centripetal Acceleration
Force is required to produce the acceleration of a body.
In a uniform circular motion, when the speed remains constant, the direction of the velocity changes at every point on the circular path.
So, the acceleration is produced along the radius called as centripetal acceleration.
The force which produces this centripetal acceleration is called as centripetal force.

Propulsion of rockets is based on the law of conservation of linear momentum as well as Newton’s III law of motion.
Rockets are filled with a fuel in the propellant tank.
When the rocket is fired, the fuel is burnt and a hot gas is ejected with a high speed from the nozzle of the rocket, producing a huge momentum.
An equal and opposite reaction force is produced in the combustion chamber, which makes the rocket project forward.
While in motion, the mass of the rocket gradually decreases, until the fuel is completely burnt out.
Since, there is no net external force acting on it, the linear momentum of the system is conserved.
Escape Velocity
At one stage, the rocket reaches a velocity, which is sufficient to just escape from the gravitational pull of the Earth.
This velocity is called escape velocity.
